title: ReChannel: Repurposing Text-to-Image Diffusion for Dense Prediction
hook: Depth maps and masks get generated as if they were images, decoded through the same interface as RGB pixels. This paper swaps that for a tiny linear head that's 2.5x faster.
key_points: Prior approaches reuse a pretrained text-to-image model's priors by encoding annotations (depth, normals, masks) into the RGB-trained VAE latent space, decoding them back out as image-like targets.
That inherits more of the generative output interface than dense prediction actually needs — dense prediction wants pixel-correct, task-native fields, not new RGB content.

ReChannel keeps the frozen DiT's patch-to-token-to-patch lattice, but maps each token to its output patch through a shared, token-local linear head — about 33K parameters, no spatial mixing, and drops the target-side decoder entirely.
Sets new state-of-the-art on trimap-free matting, KITTI depth, and referring segmentation; competitive on normals, saliency, and pose.
In a matched 4B setting, more accurate and 2.48x faster than an edit-plus-latent-decode counterpart.
content_html: Depth maps, alpha mattes, segmentation masks — none of these are pictures, exactly, but a common trick treats them like ones anyway: encode them into a text-to-image model's RGB-trained latent space and decode them back out through the same interface used for generating pictures. ReChannel argues that's borrowing more machinery than the job needs.
extra_html: The authors' key observation is that a pretrained diffusion transformer already organizes its RGB inputs through a patch-to-token-to-patch lattice on the image plane — so each token already indexes a fixed output patch, and that patch's channels could just as easily carry task-native quantities as RGB appearance. ReChannel keeps the frozen DiT and its VAE encoder for input, but drops the target-side decoder entirely, adapts the model with a task-specific LoRA, and maps each token straight to its pixel-space patch through a shared, token-local linear head — about 33,000 parameters, with no spatial mixing at all. Tested on FLUX-Klein across six dense-prediction tasks and over a dozen benchmarks, this minimal interface sets new state-of-the-art on trimap-free matting, KITTI depth, and referring segmentation, and stays competitive on normals, saliency, and pose — while being more accurate and 2.48x faster than an edit-plus-latent-decode counterpart at matched 4B scale. The lesson: dense perception can benefit from generative pretraining's priors without inheriting its generative output interface. Zanyi Wang and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: CLIP: Learning Visual Models from Language
related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

related.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
related.hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

flashcards.prompt: What's the core critique ReChannel makes of prior methods that reuse text-to-image priors for dense prediction (depth, segmentation, etc.)?
flashcards.back_html: They encode task annotations into the RGB-trained VAE latent space and decode them back as image-like targets — inheriting the generative model's output interface (rendering new RGB content) when dense prediction actually just needs pixel-correct, task-native fields on the same image plane.

flashcards.prompt: How does ReChannel read out task-native values from a pretrained diffusion transformer (DiT)?

choices.text: A shared, token-local linear head (~33K params) maps each token directly to its output patch's channels, with no spatial mixing and no VAE decoder
It fully retrains the DiT from scratch on annotated data
It still decodes through the RGB-trained VAE, just with a different loss
It replaces the DiT entirely with a CNN

flashcards.explanation_html: Since a pretrained DiT already organizes RGB inputs through a patch-to-token-to-patch lattice, ReChannel keeps that structure but swaps the target-side interface: a tiny, token-local linear head reads task-native quantities straight off each token, skipping the RGB-decoding step entirely.
